newsitem.title: USA: Clinton expects to use line-item veto on budget.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expects to use line-item veto on budget.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said Wednesday he expects to make some use of the line-item veto to strike some special tax breaks from the budget plan he signed on Tuesday.
"The short answer is there will be some exercise of that," Clinton told a news conference, referring to his new authority to strip items from spending and tax measures without vetoing an entire bill.
The White House is reviewing for possible deletion 79 tax breaks for specific companies and individuals that were included in the budget plan. Clinton has until Monday to act on those.
Clinton said he would be briefed later this week on items that could be vetoed and that he had not made up his mind yet on any of them.
But he said he would protect any items that were included in the budget plan as part of the give-and-take of negotiations between the White House and Capitol Hill, even if do look questionable.

"This was an agreement entered into in good faith and I cannot use the line-item veto on anything that our negotiators agreed to let go through," he said. "I think that's very important and I want to bend over backwards to make sure there is no misunderstanding on that."
